features.name: Captured evidence line per criterion
features.label: Captured 12:41 · you
features.promise: Each criterion records what evidence backs its verdict: who captured it, when, and the route it was captured on; where it failed the line says what actually happened instead.
features.howToVerify: Capture evidence on a criterion and confirm the meta line appears with a timestamp, your name and the route.
features.notes: Passing form: 'Captured 12:41 . you' + '/c/local/explorer/node-health' (39:1229/39:1231, 39:1254/39:1256). Failing form (39:1281): alert icon + 'It draws an empty chart with no explanation.' + '/c/imported-eu/...'. Unanswerable form (39:1324): 'Nothing here has fifty nodes. Needs a real cluster.'

features.name: Show me
features.label: Show me
features.promise: For each criterion the reviewer can press 'Show me' to have the pinned preview drive itself to the state that criterion is about.
features.howToVerify: Press 'Show me' on criterion 3 and confirm the preview on the right navigates to the relevant page and the preview header says 'Checking criterion 3'.
features.notes: Button/Neutral with a play icon, repeated on all four criteria (39:1239, 39:1264, 39:1291, 39:1332). The link to the preview header is inferred from the header reading 'Checking criterion 3', which is the criterion whose card is expanded.

features.name: Reviewer's note on a failed criterion
features.label: Your note — the author and the assistant both see this
features.promise: The reviewer can type a note explaining a verdict, and is told up front that both the author and the assistant will read it.
features.howToVerify: Type into the note field on a failed criterion, navigate away and back, and confirm the text persists and is visible to the author.
features.notes: Drawn as a bordered, rounded box with a caption label and filled-in body text (39:1298), which reads as an editable field. That it is editable rather than a rendered note is inferred from the label wording. The label uses an em dash verbatim.

features.name: Send one criterion back to the assistant
features.label: Send this back to the assistant
features.promise: A failed criterion, with its note and evidence, can be handed straight back to the AI assistant to fix.
features.howToVerify: Click it on the failed criterion and confirm the criterion is marked as sent and the assistant starts work.
features.notes: Button/Primary with a sparkle icon.

features.name: Attach a screenshot
features.label: Attach a screenshot
features.promise: The reviewer can attach their own screenshot to a criterion's note as extra evidence.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Attach a screenshot', pick a file, and confirm it attaches to the criterion.
features.notes: Button/Ghost with an upload icon. Whether it opens a file picker or a capture tool is not drawn.

features.name: Publishing blocked while any criterion is No
features.label: Publishing is blocked while any criterion is No
features.promise: The rule is stated inline next to the failing criterion: a 'No' blocks publishing; nothing says a 'Can't tell' does.
features.howToVerify: With one criterion set to No, confirm the sentence renders and publishing is actually blocked; set it to 'Can't tell' and confirm the block lifts.
features.notes: This is the design's answer to what happens to an unresolvable criterion: only No blocks.

features.name: Scope drift warning
features.label: This build does one thing the brief never mentioned
features.promise: The Studio automatically flags behaviour in the build that no criterion covers, explains it in plain language, and marks it 'found automatically'.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the amber-bordered card renders with the heading, the 'found automatically' tag and the explanatory paragraph.
features.notes: Amber stroke #C9A227. Body 39:1346 explains the 'last viewed' annotation write and that the extension is no longer read-only. Tag 39:1344.

features.name: Accept the drift into the brief
features.label: That is fine — add it to the brief
features.promise: The reviewer can accept undeclared behaviour by amending the brief to cover it.
features.howToVerify: Click it and confirm a new item appears in the brief and the drift warning clears.
features.notes: Button/Neutral. Label uses an em dash verbatim.

features.name: Remove the drifted behaviour
features.label: Remove it
features.promise: The reviewer can reject undeclared behaviour and have it taken back out of the build.
features.howToVerify: Click 'Remove it' and confirm a change is requested that strips the behaviour.
features.notes: Button/Ghost with an undo icon.

features.name: Pinned preview says which criterion it is showing
features.label: Checking criterion 3
features.promise: The live preview pane is bound to the criterion under examination and says which one, with a live dot.
features.howToVerify: Press 'Show me' on a different criterion and confirm the header text follows.
features.notes: Dot 39:1357 filled green, suggesting the preview is running.

features.name: Open the preview in its own window
features.promise: The reviewer can pop the pinned preview out of the panel into a full window.
features.howToVerify: Click the external-link icon in the preview header and confirm the preview opens standalone.
features.notes: icon/external, no text label. Its behaviour is inferred from the icon.

features.name: Choose the cluster the preview runs against
features.label: imported-eu
features.promise: The reviewer can point the preview at a different cluster, and the control annotates the current one with why it matters here ('no metrics-server').
features.howToVerify: Click the cluster row and confirm a dropdown of clusters appears, then pick another and confirm the preview reloads against it.
features.notes: Row with a server icon (39:1365), cluster name (39:1370), an annotation (39:1371) and a chevronDown (39:1373), so it is a dropdown.

features.name: Live rendered result
features.label: Node health
features.promise: The pane renders the actual running extension page, here showing the failure the criterion is about: an empty chart labelled '(nothing, and no explanation)'.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the preview canvas renders the running build rather than a static image.
features.notes: The '(nothing, and no explanation)' text (39:1382) is the mock's annotation of the empty state, not necessarily a real string.

features.name: Why evidence is captured
features.label: What you see here is captured with your answer, so nobody has to take your word for it later — and so the next person to touch this extension knows why it was rejected.
features.promise: The screen explains that captured evidence travels with the verdict and outlives this review.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the sentence renders above the capture button.
features.notes: Verbatim text uses an em dash.

features.name: Capture this as evidence
features.label: Capture this as evidence
features.promise: The reviewer can snapshot the current preview state and attach it to the criterion they are answering.
features.howToVerify: Press it while the preview shows criterion 3, then confirm that criterion's meta line gains a 'Captured HH:MM . you' entry with the current route.
features.notes: Button/Neutral with a save icon. The link between this and the per-criterion 'Captured 12:41 . you' lines is inferred from the wording.

features.name: Two-part sign-off status
features.label: Code review
features.promise: The footer shows both gates: 'Code review - Ana Silva . yesterday' complete, 'Outcome sign-off - you . in progress' still open.
features.howToVerify: Confirm the code review row shows a completed marker and the outcome row shows an empty dot with 'in progress'.
features.notes: Code review marker 39:1394 is an icon (done); outcome dot 39:1400 is an empty ellipse. Same component as screen 12's decision bar, one step further along.

features.name: Footer blocking summary
features.label: 1 criterion is not met — publishing stays blocked
features.promise: The footer counts the failing criteria and restates that publishing stays blocked while any remain.
features.howToVerify: Change the failing criterion to Yes and confirm the sentence disappears or the count drops to zero.
features.notes: Counts only the one 'No' criterion, not the 'Can't tell' one, which is the same rule as the progress chip. Verbatim text uses an em dash.

features.name: Send the whole list back
features.label: Send the whole list back
features.promise: The reviewer can return the entire criteria list, with every verdict, note and captured screenshot, to the author in one action.
features.howToVerify: Click it and confirm the change leaves the reviewer's queue and reaches the author with all four verdicts attached.
features.notes: Button/Neutral with an undo icon. Distinct from the per-criterion 'Send this back to the assistant' (39:1300).

features.name: Sign off on the outcome
features.label: It solves the problem — sign off
features.promise: The reviewer closes the outcome gate with a single primary action phrased as a judgement about the problem, not about the code.
features.howToVerify: With all criteria passing, click it and confirm the Outcome sign-off gate closes and publishing unblocks; with a criterion set to No, confirm it is disabled or refuses.
features.notes: Button/Primary with a check icon. Nothing in the mock shows it disabled even though the footer says publishing is blocked, so whether the button is blocked or only publishing is blocked is unresolved. Label uses an em dash verbatim.
